clue.text: Killer back in work, one tied up on board

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece sits inside the word for work

parts.note: toil means work

indicators.note: back tells us the word for the killer is read in reverse order

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, a killer

explanation.surface: A murderer returns to his labours, one of them a captive held on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Killer' suggests a murderer, but it is the venomous snake; 'back' reverses it, and 'in' places it within the labour word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sail is lashed or furled up aboard a ship, and this upper sail is one such canvas.

clue.text: Some part of uninspired vegetarian's diet

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an unimaginative meat-free menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd is a staple protein in vegetarian cooking, a familiar part of a meat-free diet.

clue.text: Drink gets the pub down, which is novel

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
a public house is a pub, so house can stand for it
blue means down or sad

explanation.surface: A beer makes the local feel gloomy, and that is new.
explanation.walkthrough: Porterhouse Blue is a comic novel by Tom Sharpe set in a Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sharpe wrote this 1974 satire of Cambridge college life, so it is a work of fiction.

clue.text: So positionally top-class crickets declare

parts.note: at is a preposition of position, saying where something is
a Test is international cricket at its highest level

explanation.surface: Insects of the highest quality announce something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crickets' suggests insects, but the sense is the game: Test matches are the top form of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness to something or affirm it formally is to declare it true.

clue.text: Big name for big toe?

definitions.meaning: a celebrated person, a star or famous figure
the toe is at the end of the leg, read cryptically

explanation.surface: Is a celebrity just a large digit on the foot?
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a celebrated figure, while a leg's end is the foot where the big toe lies.

clue.text: Bank is reversing into bus garage

indicators.note: into says the reversed word is placed inside the garage word

parts.note: a depot is where buses are garaged

indicators.note: reversing tells us the little word is is written backwards

explanation.surface: A bank backs its vehicle into the place where buses are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns IS into SI, which goes into DEPOT. 'Bank' is a verb: to bank money.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank money is to lodge it with a bank, which is the verb used for paying cash in.

clue.text: Hymn fades, one listener having turned up

parts.note: dies means fades away
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an ear is what listens

explanation.surface: A hymn fades out as a single listener arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having turned up' turns EAR into RAE.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval Latin sequence on the Day of Judgement is sung in the Requiem Mass as a hymn.

clue.text: Psychiatrist's head gets back into anxious teaching

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of psychiatrist
into says the word for back goes inside the word for anxious

parts.note: edgy means nervous or anxious
ago means back in time, as in years back

explanation.surface: A shrink's chief returns to nervous instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is not a reversal signal here: it means AGO, which goes into EDGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedagogy is the method and practice of instruction, the art of teaching.

clue.text: How business works flexibly, joiner having called up daughter

parts.note: supply, said like supple-y, is an adverb meaning flexibly
and is a conjunction, a joining word

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: named means called

explanation.surface: A carpenter flexibly runs his firm, having phoned his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NAMED into DEMAN, then D is added. SUPPLY here is supple + -ly.
explanation.definitionFit: Economics describes market prices as set by the balance between goods offered and wanted.

clue.text: Ferocious swimmer good during rows? Listen!

indicators.note: during says the letter sits within the rows

parts.note: tiers are rows, as of seats
hark means listen

explanation.surface: A fierce creature cuts through the water while rowers argue, so pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' reads as arguments, but it is TIERS, rows of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: This large striped predator of warm seas is a ferocious fish, a dangerous swimmer.

clue.text: I spill the beans, choked by surprisingly artful prisoners

indicators.note: choked by says one piece is gripped inside the other, like a throat being squeezed
surprisingly signals the letters turn out in an unexpected order

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing or informing, spilling the beans

explanation.surface: An informer confesses, throttled by cunning fellow inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' signals the anagram and 'choked by' the container. The surface 'I' looks like a narrator, but it is also the definition: the pronoun's grammatical name.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun 'I' is the grammatical term for the speaker alone, the single self in conjugation.

clue.text: Thin person originally filling carriage; he ate all the pies!

indicators.note: filling says the pieces are packed inside the carriage word

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
reedy means thin, slender as a reed

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of person

explanation.surface: A skinny man first squeezed into a cart, while a glutton scoffed every pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he ate all the pies' is a British football chant mocking an overweight player.
explanation.definitionFit: A glutton who scoffs everything is a greedy-guts, the very picture of one who ate the whole lot.

clue.text: See 9
Antipodean machine with multiple teats of ice water malfunctioning

indicators.note: malfunctioning says the letters are not working in the right order

explanation.surface: An Australian calf-feeding device dispenses icy water when it breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: A cowfeteria is Australian and New Zealand slang for a calf-rearing feeder with many teats.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian and New Zealand farmers use this term for a feeder letting many calves suckle at once.

clue.text: After looping the loop, Red Arrows fly from here

indicators.note: after looping says the revolutionary comes after the loop shape

parts.note: a loop is round like the letter O
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary, is a famous Red

explanation.surface: Aerobatic jets loop the loop before their display, flying from an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Arrows is the RAF aerobatic team, but here Red is CHE and the arrows are darts. The OCHE is the line darts players throw from.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the throwing line, from which the arrows are thrown at the board, has this name.

clue.text: Diagram showing the average to take to the left, gaining height

indicators.note: gaining says a further letter is added on
to the left says read right to left, backwards

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
grab means take

explanation.surface: A chart shows how the norm is swept leftwards while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the left' turns PARGRAB into BARGRAP, then H is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart using rectangular columns of varying length is a common kind of diagram.

clue.text: A fool so upstanding given to repeated musical expression

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue says the run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nit is a fool
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool, so upright, is given to repeating a musical phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' reverses the first three pieces together; 'given' is only a link before the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostinato is a short musical phrase repeated persistently throughout a piece.

clue.text: Get Paul's explosive

parts.note: to land something is to get it, as in landing a job
Paul is the setter, so Paul's is mine

explanation.surface: Fetch the explosive belonging to Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the setter of this puzzle, so 'Paul's' means MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A buried bomb that blows up when trodden on is a hidden explosive device.

clue.text: Such a hotel might be in favour of accommodating bear scoffing last of breakfast

indicators.note: accommodating says the word for in favour of houses the rest

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: scoffing says the bear swallows the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Ursa is Latin for bear, as in the constellations

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of breakfast

explanation.surface: A bear wolfing down the morning meal at a hotel, of which we approve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes the end of breakfast; 'scoffing' and 'accommodating' each nest one piece in another. URSA is the Latin bear of the constellations.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels are graded by stars, and a good but not top-grade one is rated with this many.

clue.text: River takes poem to river

indicators.note: to says the abbreviation is joined on after the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A river carries a poem downstream to another river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river in central Europe forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Sound type wanted

indicators.note: sound says the word for type is said out loud

parts.note: sort means type or kind

explanation.surface: A kind of sound was desired.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the word for type and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sought is the past tense of seek, so it means looked for or wanted.

clue.text: Zulu offering conclusions along with a nation

indicators.note: conclusions points to the final letters of Zulu and offering

parts.note: and means along with

explanation.surface: A Zulu gift arrives together with a country.
explanation.walkthrough: Zulu suggests South Africa, but the nation is in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is an East African nation, a landlocked country.

clue.text: Clothes fasteners securing border bind poorly — whatever next!

indicators.note: securing says the fasteners hold the other pieces within

parts.note: toggles are bar-shaped buttons on a duffel coat
a hem is the edged border of cloth

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Coat toggles holding a badly bound hem leave one amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' signals the anagram and 'securing' the container. Toggles are the bar-shaped buttons on a duffel coat.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment at something hard to believe, much like crying 'whatever next!'

clue.text: Bottom off bicycle part, I'm running down the hill!

indicators.note: bottom off in a down clue means the lowest letter is removed

parts.note: a wheel is part of a bicycle

explanation.surface: A cyclist loses a wheel and yells while hurtling downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of exhilaration as one speeds down a slope, an exclamation of glee.

clue.text: Again letting out? Yes!

parts.note: read as re- plus a word for renting out property, the clue describes letting again; read whole, it means freeing

explanation.walkthrough: The 'Yes!' confirms that the split reading and the plain one are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting a property out once more is re-leasing, while letting a captive out is freeing.

clue.text: Cool, hot below

parts.note: neat is slang for cool or great
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cool spot with heat underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: This poetic contraction of 'beneath' means under or below.

clue.text: Wonderful character getting thinner

parts.note: ace means excellent or wonderful
tone means character or quality

explanation.surface: A marvellous person getting slimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thinner' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: This solvent is used to dilute paint and remove nail varnish, so it acts as a thinner.

clue.text: Ending in defeat, dabbler's move rubbish

indicators.note: ending in points to the last letter of defeat

parts.note: a dabbler is a dabbling duck, and ducks waddle

explanation.surface: A hobbyist's manoeuvre ends in defeat and is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A dabbler is not an amateur here but a dabbling duck, which waddles.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly, trivial talk or writing is nonsense, which is to say rubbish.
